name: Cornelius
bio: Cornelius, a Roman centurion in Caesarea known for his devotion, prayer, and generosity to the poor, was visited by an angel who told him his prayers and alms had been remembered by God and instructed him to send for Simon Peter in Joppa. When Peter arrived, Cornelius fell at his feet in reverence, but Peter told him to stand, since he too was only a man. Cornelius explained his vision and gathered household, kinsmen, and friends to hear Peter's message about Jesus; while Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on all of them, astonishing the Jewish believers present, since Gentiles were now receiving the same gift. Peter then had them baptized, marking a turning point in the inclusion of Gentiles into the church (Acts 10:1-48).
